prompt: A discrete random variable $X$ takes the values $0, 1, 2, 3$ with $P(0) = 0.15$, $P(1) = 0.35$, $P(2) = \,?$, and $P(3) = 0.10$. What is $P(X = 2)$?
hint: A probability distribution covers every possible value of $X$. What must all of its probabilities add up to?

hints.text: A probability distribution covers every possible value of $X$. What must all of its probabilities add up to?
The total has to be $1$, so add the three known probabilities, $0.15 + 0.35 + 0.10$, and subtract that sum from $1$.

explanation: A probability distribution lists every possible outcome, so its probabilities must sum to exactly $1$.
The three known probabilities add up to $0.15 + 0.35 + 0.10 = 0.60$.
The missing probability fills the gap, so $P(X = 2) = 1 - 0.60 = 0.40$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think in percents
steps: The known outcomes cover $15\% + 35\% + 10\% = 60\%$ of all cases.
The other $40\%$ of cases must be $X = 2$.
